name: xbert-working-paper
description: Shared rendering skills that turn a structured XBert plugin payload into a Word, Excel or PDF working paper saved to your project folder. Required by every compliance and close plugin that emits a file artefact.

x-xbert.tagline: The render layer every XBert compliance and close plugin shares — structured payload in, branded working paper out.
prerequisites: Pip-installable packages: python-docx, openpyxl, reportlab (the skill installs them on first run if missing)
x-xbert.longDescription:
XBert compliance and close plugins (BAS Prep, FBT Prep, STP Finalisation, Tax Reconciliation, Close Packet, Audit Evidence Pack, and the rest) describe accounting methodology. They produce a structured payload — sections, headings, supporting figures, blocking issues, QMS metadata. This plugin owns the layer underneath: bundled Python scripts that take that payload and write a real .docx, .xlsx or .pdf to your project folder, with a verification gate that fails loudly if the file didn't open cleanly.

The three skills follow May 2026 Anthropic skill conventions: each is invoked via its slash command (`/xbert-working-paper:render-docx`, `:render-xlsx`, `:render-pdf`) or auto-discovered when a consumer plugin emits a render request. Output paths are predictable (`outputs/<run-id>/`), validation is mandatory before reporting success, and the skill body stays under 500 lines. You do not need to read this plugin's SKILL files to use the consumer plugins — Claude picks the right renderer when a compliance plugin completes.

useCases.title: Foundation for compliance plugins
useCases.description: BAS, IAS, FBT, VAT, GST-NZ, STP, Super, TPAR, MTD all emit a working-paper payload and hand off to render-docx. One renderer, one branded template family, every compliance check produces a consistent file.

useCases.title: Foundation for close plugins
useCases.description: Close Packet, Month-End Pack, FS Pack, Trial Balance Alignment, Balance Sheet Explain all use render-docx for the narrative and render-xlsx for the schedules.

useCases.title: Foundation for review plugins
useCases.description: Audit Evidence Pack and Anomaly Review hand off to render-docx with hyperlinked sections that deep-link back to the source XBerts.

benefits.title: Real files on disk
benefits.description: render-docx writes a .docx, render-xlsx writes a formula-live .xlsx, render-pdf writes a .pdf. Output path is reported back so you can open or attach immediately.

benefits.title: Verification gate is mandatory
benefits.description: Every render ends with a structured check (file exists, round-trip open succeeds, no #REF!/#DIV/0! in spreadsheets). The skill does not report success until the check returns ok.

benefits.title: One layer, every plugin
benefits.description: 30+ XBert compliance and close plugins share these three skills. Branding, footers, QMS block, output folder convention — fixed once, inherited everywhere.

workflow: Install or update this plugin alongside the consumer plugins that need it
Run a compliance or close plugin (for example /bas-prep) — it completes its readiness work and emits a working-paper payload
Claude picks render-docx (or render-xlsx, render-pdf) and runs the bundled Python script with the payload
Output file is written to outputs/<check-reference-id>/ in your project folder and the path is reported back
Verification gate runs — round-trip open + structure check — and only then is the deliverable reported complete
